page: Microsoft Azure E96pds_v6 is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by a 3.4 GHz ARM-based Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor featuring 96 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with one thread per core. The instance is configured with 672 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, along with a 128 MB L3 cache. Storage is bundled with 5,669 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity.

Benchmark evaluation demonstrates high multi-core scaling and memory subsystem throughput. In multi-threaded testing, the ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng benchmarks, bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and PassMark physics execution. Large block uncached memory reads exceed 465 GB/s, supporting key-value store performance up to 170.49 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput at 99.91 GB/s. Single-core processing performance falls in the average benchmark category across Geekbench and stress-ng tests.

The E96pds_v6 offers strong resource density by providing 96 dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, preventing execution resource contention between virtual cores. The combination of high memory allocation and bundled local NVMe storage makes the instance cost-efficient for large database and caching deployments. Primary workload fits include high-density relational database clusters, Redis caching layers, static web serving infrastructure, and multi-threaded data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E96pds_v6 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the ARM-based Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. It features 96 dedicated physical cores and vCPUs, 672 GB of system memory, and 5,669 GB of bundled NVMe SSD local storage. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded CPU performance and exceptional memory bandwidth exceeding 465 GB/s read speeds, alongside high throughput in database operations and Redis SET workloads reaching 170.49 million operations per second. Single-core performance remains in the average benchmark tier, highlighting a tradeoff optimized for parallel scaling rather than single-threaded clock speed. With high memory density and local high-speed storage, the instance delivers effective resource utilization for memory-bound applications. The E96pds_v6 is well suited for high-density database clusters, distributed caching, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing workloads.
